kinds.P: Principle: a general law you reason from

items.name: Conservation of energy
items.text: Energy is transferred between stores, never created or destroyed; work done equals energy transferred.

items.name: Conservation of momentum
items.text: Total momentum of a closed system is constant in any collision or explosion.

items.name: Conservation of charge (Kirchhoff's first law)
items.text: Current into a junction equals current out.

items.name: Kirchhoff's second law
items.text: Around any closed loop, the sum of e.m.f.s equals the sum of p.d.s (energy conservation in circuits).

items.name: Newton's second law
items.text: Resultant force equals rate of change of momentum (F = ma for constant mass).

items.name: Newton's first law and equilibrium
items.text: Zero resultant force means constant velocity; equilibrium needs zero resultant force and zero resultant moment.

items.name: Newton's third law
items.text: Interaction pairs are equal and opposite, act on different objects and are the same type of force.

items.name: Principle of moments
items.text: In equilibrium, clockwise moments equal anticlockwise moments about any point.

items.name: Vectors and independence of perpendicular motions
items.text: Vectors add head to tail; perpendicular components act independently (projectiles).

items.name: Principle of superposition
items.text: Where waves meet, the resultant displacement is the sum of the individual displacements.

items.name: Photon model
items.text: Light is emitted and absorbed in quanta of energy hf; one photon interacts with one electron.

items.name: Wave–particle duality
items.text: Particles such as electrons show wave behaviour with λ = h/p.

items.name: Resistance as V/I
items.text: Resistance is the ratio of p.d. to current; components share p.d. in series and current in parallel.

items.name: Wave model
items.text: A progressive wave transfers energy; one wavelength passes in one period, so v = fλ.
